```{r}
# Bayesian Logistic Regression

library(dplyr)
library(brms)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# Loading files
fem <- read.csv("NSFG_2022_2023_FemRespPUFData.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
male <- read.csv("NSFG_2022_2023_MaleRespPUFData.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Extracting female and male divorcees
fem_div <- fem[!is.na(fem$MARENDHX_1) & fem$MARENDHX_1 == 2, ]
male_div <- male[!is.na(male$MARREND_W1) & male$MARREND_W1 == 2, ]

# FMARNO counts marriages, if someone is divorced and FMARNO > 1, they have remarried
male_div$remarried <- as.integer(male_div$FMARNO > 1)
fem_div$remarried  <- as.integer(fem_div$FMARNO > 1)

# pulling cols to keep
factors <- c("AGE_R", "POVERTY", "TOTINCR", "HIEDUC",
             "LABORFOR", "RSCRRACE", "HISP", "remarried")

# changing col name to num_children
fem_div$num_children  <- fem_div$NUMCHILD
male_div$num_children <- male_div$NUMBIOKID

fem_div$sex  <- 1
male_div$sex <- 0

# combining to one common column list, then into a single dataset
keep <- c(factors, "num_children", "sex")

remarriage_data <- bind_rows(
  fem_div[, keep],
  male_div[, keep]
)

# standardizing col names
remarriage_data <- remarriage_data %>%
  rename(
    age = AGE_R,
    poverty_ratio = POVERTY,
    total_income_cat = TOTINCR,
    education_level = HIEDUC,
    labor_force_status = LABORFOR,
    race = RSCRRACE,
    hispanic = HISP
  )

# cleaning
# replacing NSFG special codes with NA
remarriage_data$hispanic[remarriage_data$hispanic %in% c(8, 9)] <- NA
remarriage_data$num_children[remarriage_data$num_children %in% c(98, 99)] <- NA
remarriage_data$age[remarriage_data$age >= 95] <- NA
remarriage_data$poverty_ratio[remarriage_data$poverty_ratio > 700] <- NA

# recoding hispanic: 1 = Hispanic, 0 = not Hispanic
remarriage_data$hispanic <- ifelse(remarriage_data$hispanic == 1, 1,
                            ifelse(remarriage_data$hispanic == 5, 0, NA))

# recoding labor force status: employed (1-3) vs not employed (4-7)
remarriage_data$employed <- ifelse(remarriage_data$labor_force_status %in% c(1, 2, 3), 1,
                            ifelse(remarriage_data$labor_force_status %in% c(4, 5, 6, 7), 0, NA))

# race dummies (White is the reference category)
remarriage_data$race_black    <- ifelse(remarriage_data$race == 2, 1, 0)
remarriage_data$race_aian     <- ifelse(remarriage_data$race == 3, 1, 0)
remarriage_data$race_asian_pi <- ifelse(remarriage_data$race == 4, 1, 0)

# make missing race values NA in the dummies too
remarriage_data$race_black[is.na(remarriage_data$race)] <- NA
remarriage_data$race_aian[is.na(remarriage_data$race)] <- NA
remarriage_data$race_asian_pi[is.na(remarriage_data$race)] <- NA

# keep only final modeling columns
remarriage_data <- remarriage_data[, c(
  "remarried",
  "age",
  "poverty_ratio",
  "total_income_cat",
  "education_level",
  "num_children",
  "hispanic",
  "sex",
  "employed",
  "race_black",
  "race_aian",
  "race_asian_pi"
)]

# Handling missing values
# median imputation so rows are preserved for modeling/plots
for (col in colnames(remarriage_data)) {
  if (any(is.na(remarriage_data[[col]]))) {
    remarriage_data[[col]][is.na(remarriage_data[[col]])] <- median(remarriage_data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}

# scale predictors for Bayesian logistic regression
features <- c(
  "age", "poverty_ratio", "total_income_cat", "education_level",
  "num_children", "hispanic", "sex", "employed",
  "race_black", "race_aian", "race_asian_pi"
)

remarriage_scaled <- remarriage_data
remarriage_scaled[, features] <- scale(remarriage_data[, features])

# outcome should be factor for brms logistic regression
remarriage_scaled$remarried <- as.factor(remarriage_scaled$remarried)

# priors
manual_prior <- c(
  prior(student_t(4, 0, 10), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "age"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "poverty_ratio"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "total_income_cat"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "education_level"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "num_children"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "hispanic"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "sex"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "employed"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "race_black"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "race_aian"),
  prior(normal(0, 2), class = "b", coef = "race_asian_pi")
)

# fit Bayesian logistic regression
remarriage_brm_logit <- brm(
  remarried ~ age + poverty_ratio + total_income_cat + education_level +
    num_children + hispanic + sex + employed +
    race_black + race_aian + race_asian_pi,
  family = bernoulli("logit"),
  data = remarriage_scaled,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 180,
  prior = manual_prior
)

# summary 
model_summary <- summary(remarriage_brm_logit)

# coefficient plot
# remove female, black, aian, asian/pi, and hispanic from the graph
coef_df <- as.data.frame(model_summary$fixed)
coef_df$Variable <- rownames(coef_df)

# rename CI columns
colnames(coef_df)[colnames(coef_df) == "l-95% CI"] <- "lower_ci"
colnames(coef_df)[colnames(coef_df) == "u-95% CI"] <- "upper_ci"

coef_df <- coef_df %>%
  filter(
    Variable != "Intercept",
    !Variable %in% c("sex", "race_black", "race_aian", "race_asian_pi", "hispanic")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = recode(
      Variable,
      age = "Age",
      poverty_ratio = "Poverty Ratio",
      total_income_cat = "Income Category",
      education_level = "Education Level",
      num_children = "Number of Children",
      employed = "Employed"
    ),
    Variable = factor(Variable, levels = rev(Variable))
  )

p_coef <- ggplot(coef_df, aes(y = Variable, x = Estimate)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = lower_ci, xmax = upper_ci),
    width = 0.2,
    color = "#2C7FB8",
    orientation = "y"
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#D95F0E") +
  
  labs(
  title = "Remarriage After Divorce: Bayesian Model",
  x = "Effect on Likelihood of Remarriage",
  y = NULL,
  caption = "> 0 = higher likelihood of remarriage   |   < 0 = lower likelihood of remarriage"
) +
theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
theme(
  plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
  axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 12))
)

print(p_coef)
```


```{r}
# Bayesian classification metrics
bayes_probs <- fitted(remarriage_brm_logit, summary = TRUE)[, "Estimate"]
bayes_pred <- ifelse(bayes_probs >= 0.5, 1, 0)
y_true <- as.numeric(as.character(remarriage_scaled$remarried))

TP <- sum(bayes_pred == 1 & y_true == 1)
TN <- sum(bayes_pred == 0 & y_true == 0)
FP <- sum(bayes_pred == 1 & y_true == 0)
FN <- sum(bayes_pred == 0 & y_true == 1)

accuracy <- (TP + TN) / length(y_true)
precision <- ifelse((TP + FP) > 0, TP / (TP + FP), 0)
recall <- ifelse((TP + FN) > 0, TP / (TP + FN), 0)
f1 <- ifelse((precision + recall) > 0, 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall), 0)

library(pROC)
auc_value <- auc(y_true, bayes_probs)

cat("\nBayesian Model Classification Metrics\n")
cat("Accuracy :", round(accuracy, 3), "\n")
cat("Precision:", round(precision, 3), "\n")
cat("Recall   :", round(recall, 3), "\n")
cat("F1 Score :", round(f1, 3), "\n")
cat("ROC-AUC  :", round(as.numeric(auc_value), 3), "\n")

cat("\nConfusion Matrix:\n")
cat("             Pred 0   Pred 1\n")
cat("Actual 0:   ", sprintf("%6d", TN), sprintf("%8d", FP), "\n")
cat("Actual 1:   ", sprintf("%6d", FN), sprintf("%8d", TP), "\n")
```

```{r}
cat("\nFemale divorced:", nrow(fem_div), " | remarried:", sum(fem_div$remarried, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Male divorced:", nrow(male_div), " | remarried:", sum(male_div$remarried, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

print(model_summary)

fixed_df <- as.data.frame(model_summary$fixed)
fixed_df$Variable <- rownames(fixed_df)

colnames(fixed_df)[colnames(fixed_df) == "l-95% CI"] <- "lower_ci"
colnames(fixed_df)[colnames(fixed_df) == "u-95% CI"] <- "upper_ci"

print(fixed_df[, c("Variable", "Estimate", "lower_ci", "upper_ci", "Rhat")])
```
